title: Delegate what you can verify faster than you could write
takeaway: Hand over the code that is in the way; write the part you are learning yourself, then ask for a critique.
sources: Learning happens when you retrieve something with effort, not when you recognise it as correct.
Never accept code you could not have written, without first understanding why it works.
For anything you are actively trying to learn, the worse version you wrote is more valuable than the better version you accepted.
Where verification is cheap, delegate freely.

data.question: Can you verify the output faster than you could produce it?

branches.then: Checking needs the skill being built
branches.verdict: Write it yourself, then ask for critique
